title: fix(permissions): parse unix: net rules as POSIX paths
body:
## Summary
- `--allow-net=unix:/var/run/docker.sock` is a POSIX path. `Path::is_absolute()` on Windows requires a drive letter, so `deno compile --target=linux` from Windows rejected a valid Linux unix-socket allowlist as "path must be absolute and non-empty"
- A leading `/` is parsed and lexically normalized with POSIX rules on every host (the cross-compile fix)
- Other values fall back to host `Path::is_absolute()`, so Windows named pipes (`\\.\pipe\foo`) stay expressible as a scoped `unix:` rule instead of requiring blanket `--allow-net`
- Keep rejecting empty and relative `unix:` values
- This is host-side validation only. `flags_net::parse` keeps the original string; `PermissionsOptions` is re-parsed on the target at runtime. The compile-time gate was the cross-compile failure; the parse change also affects Windows runtime matching, which is why the named-pipe fallback is required.

Fixes #36770

## Testing
- `cargo test -p deno_permissions test_net_descriptor_parse_for_list`
- spec `tests/specs/permission/unix_socket_posix_flag` (no unix gate): `deno run --allow-net=unix:/var/run/docker.sock main.ts`
- Windows parse cases: `unix:\\.\pipe\app` and `unix:C:\sockets\app.sock`

## AI usage
- An AI coding assistant was used to help analyze, implement, and test this change.
